title: Wound debridement and negative-pressure dressing

guidelineVersions: ELFT Tissue Viability wound management guideline v7.3
The Evidence-Based Principles of Negative Pressure Wound Therapy in Trauma & Orthopedics (2014)

brief.scenario: A 66-year-old has an open postoperative calf wound following drainage of an abscess. They are clinically stable and the surgical team has requested assessment for limited debridement and negative-pressure wound therapy (NPWT) on a wound model.
brief.task: Demonstrate the procedure on the model, explain decisions aloud and respond to examiner prompts. Do not perform a procedure on a real patient in this station.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Choose safe debridement and NPWT only after evaluating the wound, perfusion, infection and vulnerable structures.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Applying foam directly to an exposed vessel or proceeding with bleeding/necrosis untreated.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Inspect wound and neurovascular status, identify the exposed pulsatile structure, and stop before sharp debridement or NPWT across it.

flow: Introduce, consent, assess infection, perfusion and wound history
Examine wound bed, slough, undermining and vulnerable structures
Choose an appropriate debridement plan; recognise when sharp work is unsafe
Demonstrate model dressing safely, with protective interface and correct seal as authorised
Monitor output, bleeding, pain and infection; document review and escalation

grid.label: Systemic and local assessment
grid.pass: Checks observations, perfusion, wound history, infection and pain
grid.high: Connects ischaemia, systemic infection and MDT planning

grid.label: Wound characterisation
grid.pass: Identifies site, tissue, exudate, size, edges, cavities and slough
grid.high: Distinguishes devitalised tissue from viable structures

grid.label: Vessel/organ danger recognition
grid.pass: Recognises likely exposed vessel and avoids direct NPWT or sharp debridement
grid.high: Requests urgent senior wound/vascular review and protective strategy

grid.label: Debridement decision
grid.pass: Limits debridement to competent, indicated intervention after safety review
grid.high: Chooses alternative/autolytic approach and specialist assessment as appropriate

grid.label: Preparation and asepsis
grid.pass: Performs hand hygiene, protects tissue and confirms haemostasis
grid.high: Confirms patient, device and dressing plan with specialist team

grid.label: NPWT application logic
grid.pass: Explains no direct contact with exposed structures; dressing only after specialist protection/clearance
grid.high: Explains that this model may be unsuitable for routine NPWT now

grid.label: Monitor and respond
grid.pass: Checks seal, pain, fluid and bleeding; stops therapy and escalates significant bleeding
grid.high: Sets review triggers and plans for rapid assessment of deterioration

grid.label: Explain, record and follow up
grid.pass: Documents wound findings, contraindications, decisions and review plan
grid.high: Communicates realistic therapy limits and alternative pathways

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello. I am the core surgical trainee. May I examine your wound and explain the options, including a suction dressing if safe?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will assess your pain and arrange analgesia before any intervention.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Have you felt feverish or unwell? Is the leg increasingly painful, cold, numb or swollen?

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: No fever. It is uncomfortable, but my foot feels normal.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Observations stable; foot warm and perfused.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will measure the wound and describe the tissue, edges, exudate, depth, slough and any undermining without probing blindly.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: A red pulsatile structure is exposed beneath slough at one edge.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: That could be a vessel. I would not debride over it or place foam directly on it; I need urgent senior wound or vascular advice.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would select a safe debridement method only after assessment; with an exposed vessel I would defer sharp debridement here.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Show how you would prepare if the wound team subsequently cleared a protected application.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hand hygiene, aseptic preparation, check haemostasis, protect surrounding skin and prepare the prescribed device.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would ensure exposed vulnerable structures have an approved protective interface and specialist plan. If protection is not possible, I would not start NPWT.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The canister begins filling with bright red blood.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I stop therapy and summon urgent help, assess haemodynamics and control bleeding under senior direction.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would document findings, the decision not to proceed unsafely, and the review plan, explaining pain, bleeding and infection warnings to the patient.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Hello. I am the core surgical trainee. Before deciding whether a vacuum dressing is appropriate, I need to check the wound and circulation. May I examine it and discuss both benefits and risks?

high.speaker: patient
high.text: Yes, but I am worried about pain.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will assess and treat pain first. We can stop at any point.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Have you had rigors, spreading redness, worsening pain, new numbness, or a cold foot? Has anyone identified a blood vessel or tendon in the wound?

high.speaker: patient
high.text: No systemic symptoms; the team mentioned something delicate at the bottom.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Stable observations. Foot is warm, capillary refill normal.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I inspect and document dimensions, slough proportion, granulation, surrounding skin, drainage, depth and whether any tunnel has been explored. I will not blindly probe.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: There is a pulsatile red structure at the wound edge.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: This is a probable exposed vessel and a major bleeding hazard. I would suspend debridement and NPWT planning now, protect the site and get immediate senior surgical or vascular assessment.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Debridement is not simply removal of everything abnormal. I must assess perfusion and tissue viability and choose the least harmful method in consultation with the specialist wound team.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: A later model demonstration is requested once the site has been deemed safe.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I check haemostasis and the agreed protective interface, clean technique, contact allergy and manufacturer-specific setup, and protect the periwound skin.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I deliberately keep filler and suction away from unprotected vessels or organs. If the anatomy cannot be safely protected, I choose an alternative dressing rather than force NPWT.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: A sudden volume of bright-red blood is seen in the tubing.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I stop the system at once, call for emergency help, assess observations and manage haemorrhage with the senior team. It would be unsafe to wait until the next dressing round.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: My record will include a wound diagram, reason for withholding sharp debridement or NPWT, people consulted, patient discussion, and a definite reassessment plan.

failures.move: Failure to recognise an exposed vessel
Sharp debridement across a vulnerable pulsatile structure
Direct NPWT foam onto unprotected vessels/organs
Failure to stop therapy when brisk bleeding appears

recovery.when: If that structure may be a vessel
recovery.line: That structure may be a vessel. I am stopping the procedure and requesting senior wound/vascular assessment before proceeding.

recovery.when: If you have not yet assessed perfusion and haemostasis
recovery.line: I have not yet assessed perfusion and haemostasis; those checks must come before choosing debridement or NPWT.

knowledge.fact: Thick slough or necrotic eschar in the wound bed is listed as a caution or contraindication to NPWT, so the wound bed needs assessing and, where safe, debriding first.

An NHS wound guideline lists untreated osteomyelitis, malignant wounds, active bleeding or high bleeding risk, and exposed vessels, nerves, anastomoses or organs as NPWT contraindications or cautions.
Direct foam contact with exposed vessels, nerves or organs can cause injury or bleeding.
Bleeding must be controlled before NPWT and brisk bleeding requires immediate action.
Debridement method follows tissue, perfusion, patient factors and operator competence.

recall.think: Is this a safe wound for debridement and suction at all?
recall.say: “That pulsatile structure may be a vessel. I will stop and seek senior help.”
do: Assess perfusion, infection, haemostasis and vulnerable anatomy before touching slough.

numbers.meaning: No universal pressure setting or dressing-change interval; use the specific device and specialist prescription.

recall.trap: Foam or sharp instruments directly over exposed unprotected vessels.
recall.finish: Document a safe alternative and explicit reassessment/bleeding plan.

partner.opening: Demonstrate the procedure on the model, explain decisions aloud and respond to examiner prompts.
partner.actorBrief: Patient: stable, concerned about pain; denies systemic illness only when asked.

reveals.finding: expose a pulsatile red wound-bed structure

curveballs.safeAnswer: correct response is to suspend sharp debridement and direct NPWT.
candidate should stop suction and urgently escalate.
